questions.question: Who among the following was one of the founders of Rahnumai Mazdayasnan Sabha or Religious Reform Association?
questions.solution:
• Zoroastrian: Dadabhai Naoroji
  • Reform: This association worked for the social regeneration of the Parsi community.

questions.question: The Champaran Satyagraha took place in ________.
questions.solution:
• Year: 1917
  • Movement: Champaran was Mahatma Gandhi's first civil disobedience movement in India.

questions.question: With which of the following Government of India Acts did the Montagu-Chelmsford Reforms introduce Dyarchy in the provinces?
questions.solution:
• Act: Government of India Act, 1919
  • Fact: Also known as the Montagu-Chelmsford Reforms, this act introduced Dyarchy (dual government) in provincial councils.

questions.question: ‘Back to Vedas’ was the slogan of which Reform Movement?
questions.solution:
• Slogan: Arya Samaj
  • Context: Dayanand Saraswati gave the call 'Back to Vedas' to purify Hinduism and reject later distortions like idol worship.

questions.question: Bramho Samaj was founded by whom?
questions.solution:
• Founder: Raja Ram Mohan Roy
  • History: Established in 1828 as Brahmo Sabha, it was the first significant socio-religious reform movement in modern India.

questions.question: Who among the following, along with her close associates, started the secret congress radio during the Quit India Movement?
questions.solution:
• Secret Radio: Usha Mehta
  • Detail: During the Quit India Movement (1942), she operated the 'Congress Radio' to broadcast news that was censored by the British.

questions.question: When was a comprehensive despatch on education called Wood’s despatch on education sent?
questions.solution:
• Education: 1854
  • Fact: Wood’s Despatch is known as the Magna Carta of English Education in India and proposed a proper hierarchy of schools and colleges.

questions.question: By which of the following acts was a bicameral legislature introduced in India at the centre level?
questions.solution:
• Legislature: Government of India Act of 1919
  • Detail: This act replaced the single Council of State with a Bicameral legislature consisting of a Council of State and a Legislative Assembly.

questions.question: Magadha Mahajanapada was surrounded by the rivers _______.
questions.solution:
• Geography: Ganga and Son
  • Context: Rivers like the Ganga and Son flowed through Magadha, providing water for agriculture and a cheap means of transport.

questions.question: Which of the following organisations was established in 1885?
questions.solution:
• Organization: Indian National Congress
  • Establishment: Founded in 1885 at Gokuldas Tejpal Sanskrit College, Bombay, with W.C. Bonnerjee as its first president.

questions.question: Who among the following wrote ‘Anand Math’ from where India’s National song ‘Vande Mataram’ has been taken?
questions.solution:
• Literature: Bankim Chandra Chatterjee
  • Work: Anand Math is a historical novel based on the Sannyasi Rebellion; 'Vande Mataram' was published within its pages.

questions.question: Chittaranjan Das along with ________ set up the Swaraj Party in 1923 to contest the elections.
questions.solution:
• Political Party: Motilal Nehru
  • Context: After the suspension of the Non-Cooperation Movement, the Swaraj Party was formed to fight the British from within the legislative councils.

questions.question: Who was associated with the foundation of the Fergusson College?
questions.solution:
• Education: Bal Gangadhar Tilak
  • College: Fergusson College was founded in 1885 by the Deccan Education Society to provide affordable nationalist education.

questions.question:
Which of the following modern industries was in operation in India during the British rule?
a. Cotton
b. Jute
c. Iron and Steel
questions.option_3: All of a, b and c
questions.solution:
• Industries: All of a, b and c
  • British Era: While the pace was slow, Cotton, Jute, and Iron & Steel (like TISCO in 1907) were the core modern industries operating in India.

questions.question: Who among the following was the Maharana of Mewar and composed a book on music called ‘Sangeet Raj’?
questions.solution:
• Author King: Maharana Kumbha
  • Mewar: A great patron of arts, Rana Kumbha wrote the Sangeet Raj, which is considered an encyclopedic work on music.

questions.question: The Amara-Nayakas were ________ in Vijayanagara Empire.
questions.solution:
• Military Term: military commanders
  • Vijayanagara: The Amara-Nayakas were given territories (Amaram) to govern and were required to maintain a specific military force for the King.

questions.question: Which of the following varnas primarily used to do cultivation, animal husbandry and trade during the later Vedic period?
questions.solution:
• Social Class: Vaishya
  • Vedic Order: In the Varna system, the Vaishyas were the 'Vis' or commoners primarily responsible for producing wealth through trade and farming.

questions.question: While historians use the term Vijayanagara Empire and contemporaries of this empire described it as the_______________.
questions.solution:
• Native Name: Karnataka Samrajyamu
  • Empire: While we use the term Vijayanagara today, inscriptions of that era frequently refer to it as the Karnataka Empire.

questions.question: The Hindu Mahasabha was founded as a response to muslim fundamentalism in which year?
questions.solution:
• Year: 1915
  • Organization: The Hindu Mahasabha was established at Haridwar, with Madan Mohan Malaviya being one of its early prominent leaders.

questions.question: What was the period of Harshavardhana's reign?
questions.solution:
• Reign: 606 CE to 647 CE
  • Harshavardhana: He belonged to the Pushyabhuti dynasty and ruled most of North India from his capital at Kannauj.

questions.question: Who among the following was the founder of the Bahmani Sultanate, who took the title of Bahman Shah after his accession to the throne?
questions.solution:
• Founder: Alauddin Hasan
  • Bahmani: Also known as Hasan Gangu, he founded the first independent Islamic kingdom in South India in 1347.

questions.question: The main (chief) social unit of the Aryans was ______.
questions.solution:
• Social Unit: Jana
  • Aryan Structure: The Jana was the largest social unit (tribe), while the smallest was the Kula (family).

questions.question: Which of the four Vedas contains a collection of magic spells and charms to fend off evil spirits and diseases?
questions.solution:
• Veda: Atharva Veda
  • Fact: Unlike the other three Vedas which focus on rituals and hymns, the Atharva Veda deals with everyday life, cures, and protection from spirits.

questions.question: By what name did Allauddin Khilji build his capital?
questions.solution:
• Capital: Siri
  • Khilji Era: Siri Fort was the second of the seven cities of Delhi, built by Alauddin Khilji primarily to defend against Mongol invasions.

questions.question: In which period is the first inscriptional example of the practice of Sati found?
questions.solution:
• Inscription: Gupta
  • Sati: The Eran Inscription (510 CE) from the time of Bhanugupta provides the first archaeological evidence of the practice of Sati.

questions.question: Iron age is so named because during this time iron mostly replaced _________ in implements and weapons, beginning in the Middle East and South-eastern Europe.
questions.solution:
• Ages: bronze
  • History: The Iron Age marked a shift in human civilization as iron allowed for stronger tools and more effective farming compared to the softer bronze.

questions.question: In which year was an approach and program named Joint Forest Management (JFM) launched in the context of National Forest Policy?
questions.solution:
• Policy: 1988
  • Forestry: The Joint Forest Management (JFM) program was launched to involve local communities in the protection and management of forests.

questions.question:
The question consists of two statements, namely, Assertion (A) and Reason (R). Use them to choose the correct alternative.
Assertion (A): During the British rule, India’s exports exceeded the imports leading to surplus of balance of trade.
Reason (R): The surplus of balance of trade was used for growth and development of India.
questions.option_1: A is true and R is false
questions.option_2: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
questions.option_3: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
questions.option_4: A is false but R is true
questions.solution:
• Economic Balance: A is true and R is false
  • Analysis: While the British did maintain an export surplus, the profit was drained as 'Home Charges' and salaries, not used for India's development.
